title: Service delegation and regional routing canvas
content:
Purpose:
Quick working canvas to propose a lighter-weight service-delegation model for the control surface and region-aware routing. Goal is to reduce cross-team blast radius, make runtime adapter contracts explicit, and document minimal handoffs for multi-region failover. Not a final spec; noisy notes + decisions + next-actions.

Context / problem statement:
- We currently have ambiguous ownership overlap between API gateway, orchestrator (control plane), and runtime adapters. During region failover or capacity shortages we see ad-hoc routing changes that require SRE + platform involvement.
- Need a clear, low-friction contract so individual teams can: (a) reason about where policy lives; (b) implement fallbacks without breaking tenant isolation; (c) measure cost/latency impact per layer.

High-level design principles (working):
1) Single source of truth for routing policy should be the orchestrator control plane. Gateway only enforces ingress-level constraints and global quotas.
2) Runtime adapters own hardware-specific placement, capacity signals and pack-level admission control. They expose a small capability surface (health, capacity, variant compatibility).
3) Regional routing decisions should be expressed as declarative policies in the control plane and carried as immutable routing tokens that downstream systems consume.
4) Minimize synchronous cross-service calls during request path — precomputed routing decisions + cached adapter metadata.

Ownership map (proposed):
- API Gateway (edge-proxy team):
  - Owned by: edge-proxy squad (eng-platform).
  - Responsibilities: TLS, auth, global rate limits, simple header-based routing, metrics tagging, initial tenant affinity cookie.
  - Not responsible for: region fallback logic, model variant selection, per-request batching decisions.

- Control Plane / Orchestrator (orchestration team):
  - Owned by: orchestrator squad (eng-platform).
  - Responsibilities: central routing policy store, rollout rules (canary/A/B), per-tenant regional affinity policy, fallback policies, token generation for routing decisions, config API for gateway and runtime adapters.
  - Outputs: routing tokens, per-tenant policy blobs, rollout snapshots (versioned).

- Runtime Adapters (runtime team):
  - Owned by: runtime-adapter teams per-hosting type (hosted, dedicated, private).
  - Responsibilities: report real-time capacity/latency signals, accept routing tokens, enforce adapter-local admission (batching, concurrency), implement model variant compat checks, provide health and version compatibility endpoints.
  - Must not: trust unvalidated client-supplied routing metadata. Always validate tokens with orchestration if token nonce/version mismatch.

- Region Relay / Regional Router (multi-region infra):
  - Owned by: regional-routing subteam (eng-infra/region).
  - Responsibilities: apply region-level overrides (regulatory, emergency), perform cross-region failover orchestration when requested by control plane, and maintain topology knowledge (which runtimes are reachable).

Adapter contract (minimal, to be implemented by all adapters):
1) /healthz — liveness, version, active-variants (string list).
2) /capabilities — static: model architectures supported, quantization profiles, max-seq-length.
3) /capacity — dynamic: current slots, queued-requests, average-latency-1m.
4) token validation endpoint OR documented token schema to validate locally (public key id + nonce + signature + version).
5) admission-control: accepts inbound request metadata (routing token, tenant-id, requested-variant) and returns: proceed | queued | reject (with canonical retry-after and fallback hint).

Routing token (proposal):
- Fields (kept small): token_id, tenant_id, policy_version, preferred_region, allowed_variants (list), signature_kid, issued_at, expires_at.
- Usecases: gateway attaches token to request; runtime adapter checks allowed_variants and policy_version; region relay may override preferred_region but must attach an override flag and audit reason.

Example request flow (happy path):
1) Client -> API Gateway (edge) with tenant credentials.
2) Gateway calls orchestrator config cache (fast read, pre-warmed) to attach current routing token for tenant.
3) Gateway forwards to region-closest regional-router which maps to a runtime adapter endpoint via service registry.
4) Runtime adapter validates token locally, maps requested model to a running variant, enqueues if necessary and returns streaming response.

Example failover flow (runtime overloaded):
- Runtime Adapter returns reject with fallback hint: fallback_region=eu-west-1, fallback_variants=[gptx-8q, gptx-8q-fast].
- Regional Router consults orchestrator policy snapshot and attempts cross-region forward to fallback runtime with emergency-circuit headers.
- Orchestrator records a rollback event and publishes a short-term override (policy_version++) to the gateway config cache.

Decision notes + trade-offs captured:
- Where to store per-tenant affinity? Option A: Orchestrator policy (single source) vs Option B: Gateway sticky-cookie. Trade-off: single source stronger for rollouts, cookie cheaper for low-latency affinity. Prefer orchestrator policy stored in cache with short TTL.
- Token vs synchronous policy check: tokens preferred to avoid blocking in-path calls; however tokens must be short-lived and revocable. Implement revocation via policy_version bump + short TTL.
- Adapter-run-to-run routing: avoid heavy orchestration logic in adapters. They should indicate hints not perform global re-routing.

Operational signals & alerts (KPI proposals):
- Token-mismatch rate (requests where adapter sees unknown policy_version).
- Cross-region failover rate per tenant.
- Average time-to-failover (ms) when primary region rejects.
- Percentage of requests served by fallback variant (quality monitoring tie-in).

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- Security: finalize token signing KMS flow for private deployments (who rotates keys per-customer?). Owner: security; due: 2024-11-15.
- Caching: how large should gateway config cache be per-instance? Prototype with 10k tenant entries and measure hit rate. Owner: edge-proxy; due: 2024-11-05.
- Adapter admission API schema: finalize fields and HTTP semantics (200 vs 202 vs 4xx). Owner: runtime team; due: 2024-11-12.
- Concurrency: define a canonical backpressure header to propagate queue depth to callers so gateways can make routing decisions. Owner: orchestration; due: 2024-11-18.

Notes from discussion (internal):
- Marco: emphasized observable audit trail when region relay overrides policies; must emit structured event to event-bus.
- Emily: wants a small 'fast path' for very low-latency tenants where gateway can use cookie-only affinity and skip token fetch — propose whitelist feature in orchestrator.
- Noah: suggested embedding model quality weights in allowed_variants so orchestrator can prefer cheaper/approx variants automatically.

Sketch (ASCII):
[Client] -> [API Gateway] --(routing token)--> [Regional Router] -> [Runtime Adapter]
                          \                                /
                           \--(policy cache refresh from orchestrator) /

Audit & rollout policy:
- All policy changes are versioned and immutable; rollout uses snapshot ids; gateway & adapters must accept snapshot id and reject older versions.
- Canary rollouts: orchestrator will mark policy snapshot with percent traffic; gateways apply local sampling and adapters accept sampling header to log cohort.

Appendix: proposed git/jira names for implementation tasks:
- git: control-plane/routing-token-service
- jira: RTE-1301 implement adapter admission API
- jira: EDGE-904 gateway config cache prototype

Bottom line / next meeting agenda:
- Agree on token schema and TTL strategy (10m vs 1m) and how to revoke.
- Prototype gateway config cache with sample tenants and measure miss/hit.
- Draft adapter admission API and run a short spike to ensure no synchronous orchestration required on hot path.

This doc is intentionally rough — please add inline comments, call out missing integration points (billing, compliance), and flag anything that would block private deployment (kms/rotation, air-gapped signing).
